historical_references.reference: Urrab was a major port city on the eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, known as Hadramaut. It was an important trading center between the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa, particularly for the trade of frankincense and myrrh. Urrab was a significant cultural and religious hub for the early Islamic civilization, with numerous mosques and theological schools.

Urrab was also a key strategic military location in the Islamic expansion into East Africa. The city was a base for several Islamic naval expeditions, including the 7th/6th century CE expedition led by Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab, which helped establish Islamic presence on the eastern coast of Africa.
